author: Aubie (auto-proposed)

lesson.title: Antifragility in Nature
lesson.topic: Understanding how antifragile systems can be observed in natural phenomena and ecosystems.
lesson.steelman: How do different organisms exhibit antifragility, and what lessons can we learn from them?
lesson.steelman_for: Nature provides countless examples of antifragile systems that thrive under stress, such as the way trees grow stronger with wind resistance.
lesson.steelman_against: Some argue that natural systems are not always perfectly antifragile; they may sometimes break under extreme conditions.
lesson.example: Imagine Ana, 12, who notices that her garden's flowers bloom more vibrantly after a rainstorm, showing how they benefit from stress.
lesson.activity: Observe a local ecosystem over a few days and note how different species respond to changing conditions.
check_questions: Can you give an example of an organism that benefits from stress in nature?
How might understanding antifragility in nature help us design better systems?
What are some potential drawbacks to seeing human systems as antifragile?

rationale: This lesson helps learners connect the concept of antifragility to real-world observations, deepening their understanding and appreciation for its practical applications.
